hints: Look at the left to right direction on the x-axis from art to vein. Should blood pressure overall go up and down, or fall in one direction only?
Remember where friction is greatest. In which vessel, the narrow arterioles (a), does pressure fall most steeply, and can pressure ever rise again once energy is lost?
walkthrough:
**Recall what creates blood pressure**

Think of pressure as the push from the heart. It is highest close to the heart in the arteries (art) and energy is gradually lost as blood rubs against vessel walls.

So from art to vein, the overall trend must be a continuous fall, never a rise.

**Find where the steepest fall happens**

Arterioles (a) are very narrow and offer high resistance. This causes a lot of friction, so pressure drops most sharply there.

It then keeps falling more gently through capillaries (c), venules (v) and veins to almost zero.

**Match this shape to the graphs**

Only graph A shows a high start in art, a steep fall through a, then a gentle continuous fall through c, v and vein to near zero. That is exactly the correct pattern.

options.A: Shows highest pressure in art, steepest drop in arterioles (a), then steady fall to lowest in veins. This matches loss of energy due to friction.
options.B: Shows pressure staying high through arterioles (a) and falling mainly in capillaries. This is wrong because the greatest resistance and pressure drop is in the arterioles.
options.C: Shows pressure rising again in veins after falling. Pressure cannot rise again because the heart is the only pump and energy is not regained.
options.D: Shows a sudden drop then a large rise in veins back to near arterial pressure. Venous pressure is always the lowest, so this shape is impossible.
